metaDescription: Five phone stands compared by base weight, adjustability and portability, so video calls, recipes and photos stay steady without holding the phone.
introParagraphs: A good phone stand gives you free hands for video calls with the grandkids, recipe screens in the kitchen and shows on the nightstand. The differences between stands show up in the base: a weighted metal base tips less than a featherweight folding plastic or thin aluminum design. This guide compares five picks: the Lamicall 360 Rotation stand, the Aurasion Adjustable stand, the Nulaxy 2-pack, the Meetuo 2-pack and the POQOD 2-pack.

The spread is clear. The Lamicall has a weighted base and a two-pivot arm with a 180-degree range, the Aurasion supports phones and tablets with a reinforced base, the Nulaxy and Meetuo are aluminum folding pairs, and the POQOD weighs about half an ounce and folds flat. The POQOD works with 4 to 10 inch devices and offers five angle slots.
We evaluated each on product specs and buyer feedback rather than claiming hands-on lab work. We weighed base stability, adjustability, device and case fit, and portability.

products.name: Lamicall 360 Rotation Cell Phone Stand
products.description:
The Lamicall 360 stand is the most stable pick here, built around a large weighted base with anti-slip pads. A smooth 360-degree pivot with a click-stop sound lets you rotate between portrait and landscape. A two-pivot arm gives a full 180-degree range of angle adjustment.

The weighted base matters because light stands wobble on video calls. The click-stop pivot gives a satisfying detent so the phone stays where you set it. The tradeoff is that it is heavier and less pocketable than the POQOD, and the listing notes that it needs two hands to adjust.

It folds for storage but is not a travel stand. Compared with the Aurasion, the Lamicall gives more pivot freedom. Compared with the Nulaxy pair, it is a single stand in a lower price tier, so you pay for stability rather than quantity.
products.bestFor: Video calls and daily desk or counter use
pros: Two-pivot arm gives wide angle range

products.name: Aurasion Adjustable Phone Stand
products.description:
The Aurasion is a versatile stand with a stable reinforced base that keeps phones and tablets steady even on smooth surfaces. The listing highlights adjustable height and viewing angle for video calls, streaming, reading or working. It is sold as compatible with phones and small tablets.

The weighted base is the key feature, and the low-cost tier is attractive. The tradeoff is that the listing gives fewer exact dimensions than the Lamicall, so check fit for thick cases. It is foldable but heavier than ultralight designs.

It is simple to set up and easy to wipe clean. Compared with the Lamicall, it offers less pivot freedom but a lower price tier. Compared with the POQOD, it is steadier for tablets and heavier phones.
products.bestFor: Households sharing one stand between a phone and a small tablet
pros: Weighted base steadies phones and tablets
Works for calls, reading and streaming

products.name: Nulaxy 2-Pack Aluminum Dual Folding Phone Stand
products.description:
The Nulaxy 2-pack gives you two aluminum folding stands, one for the desk and one for the kitchen or bag. The dual folding design collapses completely and the height and angle adjust. Aluminum construction keeps the stand firm in place and supports the phone steadily.

Two stands for one purchase is the appeal, and the metal build feels more solid than thin plastic. The tradeoff is that folding stands rely on hinges, and the lightweight base can slide on slick counters. It sits in the highest price tier of this group, which is hard to justify against the Aurasion.

It folds flat into a pocket or purse. Compared with the Meetuo pair, it offers more brand polish but a higher price tier. Compared with the Lamicall, it is far more portable but less stable.
products.bestFor: Keeping one stand at home and one on the go
pros: Two aluminum stands in one pack
cons: Light base can slide on slick surfaces
Highest price tier of the group

products.name: Meetuo 2-Piece Adjustable Cell Phone Stand
products.description:
The Meetuo is a two-piece aluminum folding stand with a mechanical design that the maker says is stable and sturdy. A non-slip silicone pad keeps the phone from sliding. Height adjusts from 5 to 6.4 inches and the angle can be customized.

The silicone pad protects the phone's back and grips well. The adjustment range is modest, so it will not lift a phone to eye level. At a mid-range price tier, it is a sensible pair.

It folds for storage. Compared with the Nulaxy, it offers similar features in a lower price tier. Compared with the POQOD, it is metal and steadier.
products.bestFor: Casual watching and cooking on two counters
cons: Limited height range of 5 to 6.4 inches

products.name: POQOD 2-Pack Foldable Cell Phone Stand
products.description:
The POQOD is the lightest and cheapest pick, weighing only about half an ounce and folding completely flat. It supports 4 to 10 inch smartphones, tablets and e-readers, with five angle slots to choose from. It is sold as a two-pack for the lowest price tier.

The fixed slots make it simple, with no hinges to adjust. The tradeoff is stability: at this weight, a heavy tablet in a case can tip it, and the stand offers no height adjustment. It is best for lightweight phones and e-readers.

It slips into a wallet or bag. Compared with the Aurasion, it is far lighter but far less stable. Compared with the Lamicall, it costs less but offers fewer features.
products.bestFor: Travel and light phone use on a stable surface

buyingCriteria.explanation: A heavier base with non-slip padding resists tipping on video calls, while light plastic stands wobble. The Lamicall 360 and Aurasion have weighted bases, while the POQOD weighs about half an ounce. Add weight to the base if you use a heavy tablet in a case. If you tap the screen often, choose a weighted base.

Check the width range and weight limit including the case. The POQOD supports 4 to 10 inches while the Meetuo adjusts from 5 to 6.4 inches. Universal fit is marketing, so verify measurements. A thick case can exceed a narrow slot.

Desktop stands typically cover about 4.3 to 6.7 inches of height, while tower styles reach 9 to 18 inches for eye-level framing. The Lamicall 360's two-pivot arm gives a 180-degree angle range. Choose more height if you are on video calls. Fixed slots such as the POQOD's five are simpler but less flexible.

Foldable models carry easily but are usually lighter and less stable. The Nulaxy and Meetuo are aluminum folding pairs, while the Lamicall is heavier. Decide whether you need portability or stability. Few stands excel at both.

Silicone or rubber grip padding avoids scratches, as on the Meetuo. An open design or charging slot lets you charge during long calls. Check that the cable port is not blocked. Anti-slip feet keep the stand from sliding.

Large adjustment points and few steps suit limited dexterity. The Lamicall needs two hands to adjust, while the POQOD uses simple slots. Test whether you can set the angle one-handed. Smooth, positive detents are easier than friction hinges.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared base weight and non-slip features from the listings. The Lamicall's weighted base and the Aurasion's reinforced base scored highest, while the POQOD at about half an ounce scored lowest. Judged from specs and buyer feedback, not lab trials.

howWeEvaluated.title: Adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored height and angle range. The Lamicall's two-pivot arm and 180-degree range scored well, while the Meetuo's 5 to 6.4 inch height scored lower. Easy-to-use detents earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Device compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered stated device sizes and case friendliness. The POQOD's 4 to 10 inch range and the Aurasion's phone and tablet support scored well. Listings with vague fit claims lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: The POQOD and Nulaxy fold flat, while the Lamicall is bulkier. The strongest pick, the Lamicall, outranks the most basic, the POQOD, on stability, though not on portability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the price tier
howWeEvaluated.description: The POQOD is lowest-cost with two stands, the Aurasion balances price and stability, and the Nulaxy costs the most. We credit stands that last.

howToChoose.subheading: Weighted Base vs Folding Travel Stand

cards.label: Weighted base
cards.text: The Lamicall and Aurasion stay put on calls and handle small tablets. They are heavier and live on a counter. Best for daily use.

cards.label: Folding travel
cards.text: The POQOD, Nulaxy and Meetuo fold flat and fit in a bag, but are lighter. Recommendation: weighted for home, folding for travel.

howToChoose.subheading: For Video Calls with Family Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A heavy base, a stable arm and enough height to keep the camera near eye level. Avoid featherweight stands that shake when you tap.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Lamicall 360 offers a weighted base and a 180-degree angle range. The Aurasion is a lower-cost alternative.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use the stand daily for calls, where the Lamicall's stability pays off, or you want the Nulaxy's aluminum pair for home and work.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need a spare for the car or suitcase, where the POQOD 2-Pack at the lowest tier is enough.

faq.q: How do I choose between a weighted stand and a folding stand?
faq.a: Weighted stands like the Lamicall and Aurasion resist tipping on calls. Folding stands like the POQOD and Nulaxy travel easily but are lighter. Choose by where you use it most.
A stand is a low-cost accessory, and the lowest tier, the POQOD, is fine for light use. Spend more only if stability matters. The Aurasion is a good middle ground.

faq.q: How do I clean a phone stand?
faq.a: Wipe with a damp cloth and dry. Clean silicone pads so they keep gripping. Avoid harsh solvents on pads.

faq.q: Will a stand fit my phone case?
faq.a: Check the stated width and thickness range, since universal fit is marketing. The POQOD supports 4 to 10 inches. A thick case may need a wider slot.

faq.q: Can a stand hold a tablet?
faq.a: Some can. The Aurasion lists tablet support and the POQOD lists up to 10 inches, but heavy tablets in cases need a weighted base. Add weight to the base if needed.
A light base or slick surface is the usual cause. Choose a weighted base and non-slip pads, and avoid tapping near the edge. Plastic stands wobble more than aluminum or metal ones.
Yes if you want one at home and one in a bag. The POQOD and Meetuo packs make that cheap. If you only need one, a single weighted stand is better.
